DAX · MDAX · SDAX — Company Health & Investment Dashboard

A simple view of 159 German listed companies. Scores run from 0 to 100; higher is generally better. Updated 2026-11-10. Not investment advice.

How to read this dashboard
Financial safetyCan the company carry its debt and stay healthy? Higher is safer.
Growth potentialCan the business grow over the next 3–10 years? Higher is better.
Price attractivenessAre the shares cheap or expensive versus their own history? Higher means cheaper.
Overall appeal40% growth + 30% safety + 30% price. A high score is not a buy recommendation.

Covers the DAX 40, MDAX and SDAX. Click any company for plain-English explanations of the numbers. “n/a” means the figure was not reported or is not meaningful for that business type. The 5-year return is a what-if scenario, not a forecast.

Methodology, caveats and data notes

The dashboard reads the same data as reports/fundamentals.md. Scores are 0–100 relative comparisons across the DAX 40, MDAX and SDAX, not probabilities. Overall appeal = 40% growth + 30% safety + 30% price. Banks, insurers, utilities, telecoms, holdings, property companies, asset-light companies and market infrastructure use sector-specific scorecards.

  • Scores are not calibrated default probabilities and are not validated against a historical default/return label panel.
  • Five-year scenarios are mechanical what-if calculations, not forecasts or target prices.
  • External credit ratings, debt-maturity schedules, order backlog, market share and organic growth are incomplete for all companies; missing inputs are renormalised.
  • MDAX/SDAX scenario prices are derived from market cap / diluted shares and beta defaults to 1.0 where no DAX beta is available. A few recent listings lack enough market data for a valuation score or scenario.
  • Quarterly statements are collected for transparency but are not used in the scorecard.
  • This is a research tool, not investment advice.
